briefHtml:
NAV S$10,407,120 (-0.12% day; listed book -0.60%)

  • Biggest mover: metals roared back — silver +4.4% to ~US$67.6, gold +3.6% to ~US$4,525 (live); Sep 3 US close: GDX +4.0%, SLVP +3.2%, SILJ +2.4%.
  • Key thing: the Fed-hike trade cracked — ADP +38k (weakest since Jan), Waller leans hold, Williams sees easing inflation; Sep hike odds ~60-64% (from ~67%). Tonight's payrolls (8:30pm SGT, consensus ~+56k) decides if the rebound holds.

Portfolio moves (Sep 3 closes)

  • US ETFs: GDX +4.0% (101.49), SLVP +3.2% (41.60), SILJ +2.4% (32.39), VNM -0.8%.
  • SGX: Seatrium +1.4%, YZJ +1.3%, VICOM +1.1%, DBS +0.5% (77.95, record area); UOL -2.0%, CDL -0.9%; STI ended Aug at all-time closing high, JPM target 7,000.
  • HK: Xiaomi -2.2%, Tencent -1.2%, SMIC -0.3%; HSI 25,252.
  • Metals: spot gold printed ~US$4,545 on Sep 3; WGC: record 289t official-sector gold buying in Q2.

Insider trades (SGX/HK, 7d)

  • Singtel: six Change-of-Interest filings dated Sep 1 (directors Yong Ying-I, Yong Hsin Yue, Wee Siew Kim, Tan Tze Gay, Lim Swee Say, Lee Theng Kiat), filed with a Notice of Transfer of Treasury Shares — consistent with share-based director compensation, not open-market dealing. Source
  • Singtel also ran daily buy-backs under its S$2bn programme on Aug 28, Sep 1, Sep 2. Nothing found for other held SGX/HK names.

Congress trades

  • Quiet week: BeltwayIQ week-36 tally (Aug 31-Sep 6, in progress): 4 filings, 1 member, all sales, ~US$57k est. volume; names/tickers not shown publicly. Source
  • No new named trades beyond yesterday's item: Rep. Michael Rulli (R-OH) sold GOOGL US$50,001-100,000 (traded Aug 24).

Trump / policy watch (24-48h)

  • Fed: ADP +38k; Waller leans hold; Williams: inflation easing as tariff effects fade; hike odds ~60-64%; payrolls tonight 8:30pm SGT (consensus ~+56k, July was -23k).
  • Tariffs: Trump slaps up to 100% tariffs on foreign-made drones (Sep 3); Canada counter-tariffs on C$27.6bn of US goods effective Sep 8.
  • Iran/Hormuz: two tankers mined in the strait; Trump: demined, "zero tolerance"; aides working to cap escalation before Nov 3 midterms; new "economic asphyxiation" sanctions; Lloyd's £1.4bn war loss; US diesel at 4-yr high.
  • AI: Nvidia agrees US$13bn deal for Hugging Face; HPE record quarter; Broadcom -5% after modest beat.
  • Portfolio corporate: Singtel-KKR completed S$6.6bn STT GDC acquisition (Sep 2).

Risk

  • Watcher riskFlags: none today. Silver rebound rebuilt the leveraged-line cushion.
  • Leveraged silver (IBKR): 1,777 oz ~S$152k vs ~S$56,240 loan (~1.5x); equity ~S$96k. Hot payrolls tonight likely retests US$64-65 silver support.
  • FX: ~35% of net worth non-SGD; SGD firming (1.2712 to 1.2670 in a day) erodes USD/HKD/CNY sleeves in SGD terms.
  • Concentration: ~62% of liquid book idle cash while STI makes all-time highs — opportunity cost now visible; DBS at record high; Astral NAV stale (Apr 30).
  • Event risk: NFP tonight + Hormuz headlines + Canada tariffs Sep 8 into Monday's Asia open.

Alpha — signals, not advice

  • GDX/SILJ/SLVP: flush reversed on the Fed-hike crack; sleeve ~4% vs 20% target. Weak NFP (<56k) confirms the add zone; hot NFP gives a second, better entry. Chart repair needs silver above US$67.2.
  • SMIC / Xiaomi: US AI capex accelerating (NVDA US$13bn Hugging Face, HPE record) while Asia AI lags (SMIC -0.3%, Xiaomi -2.2%); AI-bottleneck target 15% vs ~1% filled — relative-value accumulation zone.
  • US duration/TIPS: 10y round-tripped 4.81% to 4.76%; a hot-NFP spike toward 4.9-5.0% is the designated entry zone for the 15% defense sleeve — decide the trigger before the number.

trumpWatch.title: Fed-hike trade cracks on soft ADP + dovish pushback
trumpWatch.detail: ADP August +38k (weakest since Jan; manufacturing -17k); Fed governor Waller leans toward holding rates; NY Fed's Williams sees inflation easing as tariff effects fade. September hike odds slipped to ~60-64% from ~67%; dollar -0.7%, 10y to 4.76%. August payrolls tonight 8:30pm SGT (consensus ~+56k; July -23k) is the decider for the metals rebound.

trumpWatch.title: Trump tariffs up to 100% on foreign-made drones
trumpWatch.detail: New tariffs of up to 100% on foreign-made drones announced Sep 3 — defense/tech supply-chain theme relevant to the AI-bottleneck and defense sleeves.

trumpWatch.title: Iran/Hormuz escalation management
trumpWatch.detail: Two tankers struck by mines in the Strait of Hormuz; Trump declared the strait demined with 'zero tolerance' for new mines. Senior aides working to prevent escalation before the Nov 3 midterms, with a more aggressive posture reportedly on the table after the vote. New 'economic asphyxiation' sanctions unveiled; Lloyd's estimates £1.4bn war loss; US diesel at four-year high. WTI ~US$91.5.

trumpWatch.title: Nvidia US$13bn Hugging Face deal
trumpWatch.detail: Nvidia agreed a US$13bn deal for AI platform Hugging Face; HPE posted a record quarter with upsized guidance; Broadcom beat modestly and fell ~5% after the bell. AI capex buildout continues despite the rates scare.

trumpWatch.title: Canada counter-tariffs effective Sep 8 (reminder)
trumpWatch.detail: C$27.6bn of US imports targeted from Monday Sep 8, dollar-for-dollar response to US Section 338 tariffs; steel/aluminum counter-tariffs rise 25% to 50%.

opportunities.thesis: Real-assets sleeve ~4% of NAV vs 20% barbell target; the two-day flush reversed exactly on the Fed-hike crack (GDX back above US$100, silver ~US$67.6), validating that the selloff was rates-driven, not thesis-driven.
opportunities.signal: Tonight's NFP: weak print (<56k) likely collapses hike odds and confirms the add zone; hot print produces a second flush and a better entry. Chart repair needs silver above US$67.2. Signals, not advice.

opportunities.thesis: AI-bottleneck target 15% vs ~1% filled; US AI capex keeps accelerating (NVDA US$13bn Hugging Face, HPE record quarter) while Asia-listed AI hardware lags the US tape (SMIC -0.3%, Xiaomi -2.2% on Sep 3).
opportunities.signal: Divergence between US AI capex headlines and HK-listed AI names is a relative-value accumulation zone, not a fundamentals problem. Signals, not advice.

opportunities.thesis: Defense (duration/TIPS) target 15% vs ~0% filled; 10y UST round-tripped 4.81% to 4.76% on the data, showing both sides of the trade are live.
opportunities.signal: A hot NFP tonight that spikes the 10y toward 4.9-5.0% is the designated entry zone for the 15% defense target; a weak NFP means duration rallies away — decide the trigger before the number. Signals, not advice.
